title: Sagittarius Symbol: Copy & Paste ♐ — The Archer Pointing at the Galaxy's Core
meta_description: Copy and paste the Sagittarius zodiac symbol (♐) and the centaur myth behind it, plus the real astronomical fact that its ‘Teapot’ star pattern points straight at the Milky Way's galactic center. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
hero_tagline: Sagittarius's glyph (♐) is an arrow drawn across a bow — usually tied to the centaur Chiron, and its constellation's ‘Teapot’ star pattern happens to point directly at the black hole in the center of our galaxy. Click any symbol to copy it instantly.
intro: The Sagittarius symbol (♐, U+2650) is an arrow crossing a bow. The most common myth behind it is the centaur Chiron — tutor to the hero Achilles, who traded away his own immortality to free Prometheus and was placed among the stars by Zeus in gratitude (a rival account from the ancient astronomer Eratosthenes instead names the satyr Crotus, credited as the inventor of archery). Independent of the mythology, the constellation has a real astronomical claim to fame: its ‘Teapot’ star pattern points almost directly at the center of the Milky Way, the location of the supermassive black hole Sagittarius A*. Sagittarius runs November 22–December 21, is ruled by Jupiter, and is a Fire sign with Mutable modality.
